description: §17.6.2 — a bare expression statement inside an if-as-expression arm body is a SIDE EFFECT. It does not initialize `~`, does not rebind the tilde context, and does not touch the arm's result; only a `lift` (or the §17.6.10 single-expression sugar) designates the result value. Every function here puts one or more statements ahead of the designating form, in the `then` arm (`#out-then-lift`), in the `else` arm (`#out-else-lift`), against a sugar `else` (`#out-sugar-else`), across an `else if` cascade (`#out-cascade`), with three leading statements (`#out-multi`), with no `else` at all (`#out-no-else`), and at a `let` binding site (`#out-let`). Each renders the value the selected arm designates, not empty.
rationale: SPEC answered this question twice and disagreed with itself. §17.6.2 says an arm body "MAY contain … function calls" and that "other statements are side effects or intermediate computation"; §32.2's general rule says "An expression statement whose value is not bound to any identifier SHALL initialize `~`", which with §32.3's exactly-once rule would make `{ note("a") lift "pos" }` an E-TILDE-002. The S395 ruling settled it on specific-over-general: §17.6.2 governs INSIDE an arm body, and §32.2 now carries an explicit arm-body carve-out. Before the fix this was silent-wrong at exit 0 with ZERO diagnostics: the leading statement fell through to the shared `bare-expr` handler, which under an active tilde context minted a FRESH `let _scrml_tilde_N = <expr>;` AND rebound the context to it, so the arm's `lift` wrote the WRONG variable and the binding stayed at its `= null` seed — every `#out-*` selector below rendered EMPTY. The `else`-arm defect was worse than a wrong value: the else limb assigned a name block-scoped to the THEN branch, which in the emitted classic script (no "use strict", no type="module") is a silent implicit global rather than a ReferenceError. This is the statement+`lift` sibling of ctrl-023/ctrl-024, which pin the same binding-site question for the §17.6.10 sugar (g-bare-expr-in-if-arm-rebinds-tilde-context-corrupting-the-result-var, HIGH). §17.6.8 grants the compiler latitude over the emitted JavaScript, so this case asserts OBSERVABLE RESULTS, not emitted-code shape. `notCodePrefixes` carries E-TILDE- as a forward guard: under the ruling this shape is conforming, so §32's enforcement must never reject it if and when that enforcement starts firing.
